claims.text: The governing distance measurement is the GPS polyline, not the rounded trip-record copy: the trace on EV-GPS-00104 measures 34.17 km against a booked optimal of 27.1 km recorded on EV-TRIP-00104, an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.09% of optimal. That exceeds both limbs of the POL-RD-01 establishment test (greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km absolute), so the route deviation is ESTABLISHED on the rider's side of the case.

The threshold is comfortably passed and is not near the line: 7.07 km of excess against a materiality gate of 8.0 km and 50% under POL-RD-01, so this is an established but non-material deviation. The rider states that plainly and does not claim a materiality uplift.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-00104, the trace runs 20:35:10 to 21:22:10 from the recorded pickup event to the recorded dropoff event, and the excess is measured from a trace that is not impaired. The burden therefore shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause; a general assertion that traffic was bad does not discharge it.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07. It carries 283 fixes across the whole trip at a 10 second sample interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. None of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires, so the excess stands at the measured figure and the case cannot be diverted into an ESCALATE on trace-integrity grounds.

POL-RD-04 cannot be run against the rider. The chat log shows the diversion announced by the DRIVER ('accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok') and the rider's only reply was 'ok but not too long ah'. Limb (a) of POL-RD-04 requires the instruction to come from the rider, and the rider's message identifies no place and no road and carries no waypoint_hint, so the corroboration test cannot be run and no distance is excluded on this ground. The rider's qualified 'not too long' is also not consent to a 34 km routing.

POL-RD-05 gives the driver nothing: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so there was no relocated pin or amended endpoint and no re-baselining of the optimal route. The baseline for POL-RD-01 remains the booked 27.1 km.

POL-RD-12 does not apply: the vehicle type on this trip is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null. There is no matched pooled itinerary to measure against, so the matched-itinerary baseline the clause creates is unavailable and the booked optimal distance governs.

POL-RD-11 does not close off the distance refund: the fare model on EV-FARE-00104 is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so this is not an upfront-quoted trip and the rider is not already whole on distance and time. The POL-RD-02 arithmetic governs.

Taking the driver's PIE advisory at its highest, POL-RD-03 exonerates only part of the excess and it is capped. The justified excess is min(7.07, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = min(7.07, 4.90) = 4.90 km, giving a closure-adjusted optimal of 32.00 km. That leaves 2.17 km of excess the driver drove beyond anything the advisory can excuse, and POL-RD-03 requires that uncapped excess to be refunded under POL-RD-02 against the adjusted optimal route.

The refund on the closure-adjusted route is arithmetic. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x 1.0) + 0.80 = 39.828. Charged_total is 43.41 and the refund before rounding is 3.582, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 as SGD 3.60. The rider asks for that figure, which is what the fare breakdown's own closure computation produces against the adjusted optimal.

The driver's second traffic advisory is impaired and must be disclosed as such: EV-ADVIS-00104-02 carries weight_multiplier 0.25 with issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE, was entered through the operator console rather than the LTA feed, and its geometry covers the CTE between Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 and the SLE, where the trace contains no fix at all and intersects_route is false. POL-RD-03 requires the advisory to name a road or segment the optimal route traverses - this trip's optimal is PIE westbound throughout - so the CTE breakdown assertion excuses no distance under POL-RD-03 and carries no weight under POL-RD-08.

The rider does not seek a repeat-deviation uplift under POL-RD-06, because the record does not support one. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 288, a ratio of roughly 0.0035, well below the 0.05 ratio and the three-flag count the clause requires, and the excess remaining after the POL-RD-03 cap is non-material. The rider notes this so that the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags cannot be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure, which POL-GEN-01 forbids.

No POL-RD-09 pass-through correction is sought and none is available: the fare breakdown shows no ERP gantries, tolls_erp of 0.00 and an airport_surcharge of 0.00, on a trip that neither starts nor ends at an airport. There is accordingly no separate ERP line to add on top of the POL-RD-02 figure, and the whole of the rider's remedy is the distance and time correction of SGD 3.60.

POL-RD-10 is not engaged and the case should be decided on the merits with money moving rather than escalated. The three artifacts agree on the trip identifier, their timestamps are causally ordered and do not run backwards, the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07, every fare line reconciles to the cent, the refund is far under SGD 150.00 and the deciding artifacts all sit at weight 1.0, so the confidence floor in POL-RD-10(1) is not breached and no other trigger in that clause fires.

The diversion is exonerated under POL-RD-03. LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01, COMPLETE, weight 1.0) names the Pan Island Expressway towards Tuas, after the Eunos Link exit - the exact corridor the booking optimal used, which the trip record records as 'PIE westbound throughout'. Its validity window 20:02-21:35 brackets the trip (20:35-21:22), and the GPS trace leaves the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4, ahead of the blocked segment, and rejoins on the AYE. Limbs (a) road traversed by the optimal route, (b) window overlapping the passage, and (c) leave-before / rejoin-after are all satisfied, so the deviation is exonerated to the extent of the cap.

POL-RD-03 caps that exoneration at the lesser of the measured excess and 130% of the alternative's additional distance plus 1.0 km of tolerance: min(7.07, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = min(7.07, 4.90) = 4.90 km. So 4.90 km of the 7.07 km measured excess is justified and is not the driver's to answer for; only the 2.17 km sitting beyond the cap can ever be refundable. The rider's framing of the whole 7 km as an unjustified detour ignores this cap.

The excess of 7.07 km / 26.09% clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gates of 0.8 km and 20% but falls short of the MATERIAL gates of 8.0 km and 50%. The deviation is therefore not material, the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged at all, and the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) is unavailable on this trip. Even were it consulted, the permitted counters show driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d = 1 against 288 completed_trips_90d - nowhere near the 3 flags (or 0.05 ratio with 40+ trips) that POL-RD-06 requires to establish a pattern.

After exoneration, the residual 2.17 km is refunded under POL-RD-02 computed against the POL-RD-03 closure-adjusted optimal of 32.00 km and 40.1 min (34.0 min scaled by 32.00/27.1). Recomputed fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x 1.0 + 0.80 = 39.828; refund = 43.41 - 39.828 = 3.582, rounded UP to SGD 3.60. That is 8.25% of the charged total - nowhere near the 90% full-refund share - and a small fraction of the $14 the rider claims. The driver does not dispute the rider's 27 km baseline; the booked optimal was 27.1 km.

The chat log corroborates the exculpatory event and shows the rider was on notice in real time: at 20:38:12 the driver wrote 'accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok', matching the advisory corridor, and the rider read it and replied 'ok but not too long ah' at 20:38:55 without directing any other route or objecting. That contemporaneous assent is inconsistent with the rider's later characterisation of the route as wholly unaccountable, and to the extent the record shows the rider's own assent to the ECP routing it engages POL-RD-04 as well.

The driver's statement also mentions a CTE breakdown, and the driver does not rest on it. The only CTE advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00104-02, is IMPAIRED at weight 0.25 with issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE (it was operator-entered, not LTA-ingested, and no trace fix lies inside its geometry). It reports intersects_route false and covers the CTE between Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 and the SLE, a corridor this trip never enters. Under POL-RD-03 an advisory covering a corridor the optimal route never uses exonerates nothing, so the CTE point is discarded and the driver's case stands on the clean PIE advisory alone.

Nothing on this record engages the mandatory-escalation triggers in POL-RD-10: the trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) (100% coverage, maximum gap 0 s, steady 10 s sampling); no timestamps disagree or run backwards; the computed refund of $3.60 is far below the $150 ceiling; and no charge line is unmatched (ERP is zero throughout). The case is ripe for a monetary ruling and should not be held.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The drive was longer than the booking: the GPS trace EV-GPS-00104 measures 34.17 km from the recorded pickup to the recorded dropoff, against a booked optimal of 27.1 km on EV-TRIP-00104 — an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.09% of optimal. That clears both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%), so the deviation is established. It does not clear the material gates (8.0 km or 50%), so this is a non-material deviation; POL-RD-06 is not engaged on this trip and no repeat-deviation uplift is available.

On the driver's explanation. The PIE advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01, LTA DataMall, weight 1.0) names the Pan Island Expressway towards Tuas after the Eunos Link exit — the corridor the booking optimal actually used — and its 20:02–21:35 window brackets the trip (20:35–21:22). The trace leaves the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4, before the blocked segment, and rejoins at the AYE. That satisfies POL-RD-03, so the diversion itself is exonerated. But the exoneration is capped: the justified excess is min(7.07, 1.30 × (30.1 − 27.1) + 1.00) = min(7.07, 4.90) = 4.90 km, giving a closure-adjusted optimal of 32.00 km and 40.1 min (34.0 min scaled by 32.00/27.1). The 2.17 km driven beyond that cap is not excused.

The refund is therefore arithmetic under POL-RD-02 against the adjusted optimal, not against the booked one. recomputed fare = (3.80 + 0.75 × 32.00 + 0.28 × 40.1) × 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee = 39.828. Charged total was 43.41 (EV-FARE-00104), so the refund is 43.41 − 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, i.e. SGD 3.60. That is above the 0.50 de-minimis floor and far below the 90% full-refund share, so this is a partial refund. It is well short of the $14 the rider expected, because the closure genuinely excuses most of the extra distance.

Points on which the parties are answered together. POL-RD-04 is unavailable, as the rider correctly says: the diversion was announced by the DRIVER, the rider's only message was 'ok but not too long ah', and the rider named no place or road and left waypoint_hint null, so the rider-instruction limb and its corroboration test cannot be run. The driver's suggestion that the rider's assent engages POL-RD-04 is rejected on that ground — the chat is notice and contemporaneous assent, not an instruction that excludes distance. POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 and POL-RD-12 do not apply: there was no amended pickup or dropoff, the fare model is METERED with a null quoted fare, the vehicle type is RYDE_X and solo_optimal_distance_km is null. POL-RD-09 yields nothing to correct: no ERP gantries, tolls of 0.00 and no airport surcharge, so no standalone pass-through line is added on top of the refund. The CTE breakdown the driver mentioned is supported only by EV-ADVIS-00104-02, which is impaired at weight 0.25 with issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE (operator-entered, no trace fix in its geometry, intersects_route false); it covers a corridor this trip never enters, so it excuses nothing and no part of this ruling rests on it.

On escalation, POL-RD-10 is not engaged. The trip identifiers match across the trip record, trace and fare breakdown; the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c) (283 fixes, 100% coverage, 10 s sampling, zero gaps); the timestamps are causally ordered; every fare line has a counterpart; and the refund is far below the SGD 150 ceiling. The deciding artifacts — EV-GPS-00104, EV-TRIP-00104, EV-FARE-00104 and EV-ADVIS-00104-01 — all sit at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0 and the 0.70 floor is not approached. No referral is produced: POL-RD-06(c) needs an established repeat pattern (deviation_flags_90d is 1 against 288 trips, and prior_deviation_flags is a context-only lifetime counter that POL-GEN-01 forbids using here) and POL-RD-09(4) needs an unmatched charge line, of which there is none. The ruling is to refund SGD 3.60 to the rider; the balance of the charge stands.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides agree on the core arithmetic, and the rider is owed a partial refund of SGD 3.60 out of the SGD 43.41 charged (charged_total, EV-FARE-00104).

Deviation. The trip ran from Our Tampines Hub to Fusionopolis, one-north. The booked optimal was 27.1 km (EV-TRIP-00104) and the GPS trace measured 34.17 km (EV-GPS-00104, which governs over the rounded 34.2 km trip-record copy under POL-RD-01). The measured excess is 7.07 km, or 26.09% of optimal. That clears both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km), so a deviation is ESTABLISHED. It does not reach the materiality gates (50% or 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged and no repeat-deviation uplift or driver-conduct referral arises. On the rider's POL-RD-06 point: the citable counters (deviation_flags_90d = 1 against 288 completed trips in 90 days) show no pattern anyway, and the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags was correctly excluded as context-only under POL-GEN-01.

Exoneration, capped. The driver is largely excused. LTA advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01, weight 1.0, LTA DataMall) names the PIE towards Tuas after the Eunos Link exit — the corridor the optimal route used (PIE westbound throughout); its window 20:02–21:35 brackets the trip; and the trace left the PIE before the blocked segment and rejoined on the AYE. All three POL-RD-03 limbs are met. But the exoneration is capped at min(7.07, 1.30 × (30.1 − 27.1) + 1.00) = m(7.07, 4.90) = 4.90 km justified. That leaves 2.17 km the driver drove beyond anything the advisory excuses. The driver's claim to full exoneration is rejected as to that residual; the rider's acceptance of the 4.90 km cap is accepted.

Refund arithmetic. POL-RD-03 directs the residual to be refunded under POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal of 32.00 km (27.1 + 4.90) and 40.1 min. recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 × 32.00 + 0.28 × 40.1) × 1.0 (surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-00104) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP = 39.828. Refund = 43.41 − 39.828 = 3.582, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 3.60. It is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below the 90% full-refund share, so PARTIAL_REFUND, not FULL_REFUND.

Points rejected on the merits. (1) The driver's second advisory, EV-ADVIS-00104-02, is IMPAIRED: weight_multiplier 0.25, issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE. It covers the CTE between Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 and the SLE, a corridor this trip never enters (intersects_route false), and it was operator-entered rather than LTA-ingested. Under POL-RD-03 an advisory for a corridor the optimal route never uses exonerates nothing, so the CTE-breakdown assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. It is not a carrier of any deciding fact, so it does not enter the confidence cap. (2) The driver's suggestion that the rider's reply 'ok but not too long ah' engages POL-RD-04 is rejected: POL-RD-04 requires the instruction to come from the rider and to name a place or road specifically enough to act on, and this message does neither, with waypoint_hint null; the diversion was announced by the driver, so POL-RD-04 cannot be run and no distance is excluded on that ground. (3) POL-RD-05 gives nothing (no endpoint amended; amended_optimal_distance_km is null), POL-RD-11 does not apply (fare model METERED, quoted_fare_sgd null), and POL-RD-12 does not apply (vehicle type RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL; no solo_optimal figure). (4) POL-RD-09 gives nothing further: no ERP gantries, tolls_erp 0.00 and airport_surcharge 0.00, so there is no pass-through line to add and no billing-integrity defect to refer.

Escalation not engaged. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)–(c): 283 fixes at a steady 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s. Trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; timestamps are causally ordered; every fare line reconciles; the refund is far under SGD 150.00. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires, so we rule on the merits with money moving rather than holding the case. Confidence rests on the deciding artifacts EV-GPS-00104, EV-TRIP-00104, EV-FARE-00104 and EV-ADVIS-00104-01, all at weight 1.0, so the cap is 1.0 and the finding is comfortably above the 0.70 floor.

The rider notes this so that the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags cannot be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure, which POL-GEN-01 forbids.

ledger.claim: The governing distance measurement is the GPS polyline, not the rounded trip-record copy: the trace on EV-GPS-00104 measures 34.17 km against a booked optimal of 27.1 km recorded on EV-TRIP-00104, an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.09% of optimal. That exceeds both limbs of the POL-RD-01 establishment test (greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km absolute), so the route deviation is ESTABLISHED on the rider's side of the case.

The threshold is comfortably passed and is not near the line: 7.07 km of excess against a materiality gate of 8.0 km and 50% under POL-RD-01, so this is an established but non-material deviation. The rider states that plainly and does not claim a materiality uplift.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-00104, the trace runs 20:35:10 to 21:22:10 from the recorded pickup event to the recorded dropoff event, and the excess is measured from a trace that is not impaired. The burden therefore shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause; a general assertion that traffic was bad does not discharge it.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07. It carries 283 fixes across the whole trip at a 10 second sample interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. None of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires, so the excess stands at the measured figure and the case cannot be diverted into an ESCALATE on trace-integrity grounds.

POL-RD-04 cannot be run against the rider. The chat log shows the diversion announced by the DRIVER ('accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok') and the rider's only reply was 'ok but not too long ah'. Limb (a) of POL-RD-04 requires the instruction to come from the rider, and the rider's message identifies no place and no road and carries no waypoint_hint, so the corroboration test cannot be run and no distance is excluded on this ground. The rider's qualified 'not too long' is also not consent to a 34 km routing.

POL-RD-05 gives the driver nothing: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so there was no relocated pin or amended endpoint and no re-baselining of the optimal route. The baseline for POL-RD-01 remains the booked 27.1 km.

POL-RD-12 does not apply: the vehicle type on this trip is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null. There is no matched pooled itinerary to measure against, so the matched-itinerary baseline the clause creates is unavailable and the booked optimal distance governs.

POL-RD-11 does not close off the distance refund: the fare model on EV-FARE-00104 is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so this is not an upfront-quoted trip and the rider is not already whole on distance and time. The POL-RD-02 arithmetic governs.

Taking the driver's PIE advisory at its highest, POL-RD-03 exonerates only part of the excess and it is capped. The justified excess is min(7.07, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = min(7.07, 4.90) = 4.90 km, giving a closure-adjusted optimal of 32.00 km. That leaves 2.17 km of excess the driver drove beyond anything the advisory can excuse, and POL-RD-03 requires that uncapped excess to be refunded under POL-RD-02 against the adjusted optimal route.

The refund on the closure-adjusted route is arithmetic. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x 1.0) + 0.80 = 39.828. Charged_total is 43.41 and the refund before rounding is 3.582, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 as SGD 3.60. The rider asks for that figure, which is what the fare breakdown's own closure computation produces against the adjusted optimal.

The driver's second traffic advisory is impaired and must be disclosed as such: EV-ADVIS-00104-02 carries weight_multiplier 0.25 with issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE, was entered through the operator console rather than the LTA feed, and its geometry covers the CTE between Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 and the SLE, where the trace contains no fix at all and intersects_route is false. POL-RD-03 requires the advisory to name a road or segment the optimal route traverses - this trip's optimal is PIE westbound throughout - so the CTE breakdown assertion excuses no distance under POL-RD-03 and carries no weight under POL-RD-08.

The rider does not seek a repeat-deviation uplift under POL-RD-06, because the record does not support one. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 288, a ratio of roughly 0.0035, well below the 0.05 ratio and the three-flag count the clause requires, and the excess remaining after the POL-RD-03 cap is non-material. The rider notes this so that the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags cannot be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure, which POL-GEN-01 forbids.

There is accordingly no separate ERP line to add on top of the POL-RD-02 figure, and the whole of the rider's remedy is the distance and time correction of SGD 3.60.

POL-RD-10 is not engaged and the case should be decided on the merits with money moving rather than escalated. The three artifacts agree on the trip identifier, their timestamps are causally ordered and do not run backwards, the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07, every fare line reconciles to the cent, the refund is far under SGD 150.00 and the deciding artifacts all sit at weight 1.0, so the confidence floor in POL-RD-10(1) is not breached and no other trigger in that clause fires.

The diversion is exonerated under POL-RD-03. LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01, COMPLETE, weight 1.0) names the Pan Island Expressway towards Tuas, after the Eunos Link exit - the exact corridor the booking optimal used, which the trip record records as 'PIE westbound throughout'. Its validity window 20:02-21:35 brackets the trip (20:35-21:22), and the GPS trace leaves the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4, ahead of the blocked segment, and rejoins on the AYE. Limbs (a) road traversed by the optimal route, (b) window overlapping the passage, and (c) leave-before / rejoin-after are all satisfied, so the deviation is exonerated to the extent of the cap.

POL-RD-03 caps that exoneration at the lesser of the measured excess and 130% of the alternative's additional distance plus 1.0 km of tolerance: min(7.07, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = min(7.07, 4.90) = 4.90 km. So 4.90 km of the 7.07 km measured excess is justified and is not the driver's to answer for; only the 2.17 km sitting beyond the cap can ever be refundable. The rider's framing of the whole 7 km as an unjustified detour ignores this cap.

The excess of 7.07 km / 26.09% clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gates of 0.8 km and 20% but falls short of the MATERIAL gates of 8.0 km and 50%. The deviation is therefore not material, the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged at all, and the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) is unavailable on this trip. Even were it consulted, the permitted counters show driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d = 1 against 288 completed_trips_90d - nowhere near the 3 flags (or 0.05 ratio with 40+ trips) that POL-RD-06 requires to establish a pattern.

After exoneration, the residual 2.17 km is refunded under POL-RD-02 computed against the POL-RD-03 closure-adjusted optimal of 32.00 km and 40.1 min (34.0 min scaled by 32.00/27.1). Recomputed fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x 1.0 + 0.80 = 39.828; refund = 43.41 - 39.828 = 3.582, rounded UP to SGD 3.60. That is 8.25% of the charged total - nowhere near the 90% full-refund share - and a small fraction of the $14 the rider claims. The driver does not dispute the rider's 27 km baseline; the booked optimal was 27.1 km.

The chat log corroborates the exculpatory event and shows the rider was on notice in real time: at 20:38:12 the driver wrote 'accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok', matching the advisory corridor, and the rider read it and replied 'ok but not too long ah' at 20:38:55 without directing any other route or objecting. That contemporaneous assent is inconsistent with the rider's later characterisation of the route as wholly unaccountable, and to the extent the record shows the rider's own assent to the ECP routing it engages POL-RD-04 as well.

The driver's statement also mentions a CTE breakdown, and the driver does not rest on it. The only CTE advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00104-02, is IMPAIRED at weight 0.25 with issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE (it was operator-entered, not LTA-ingested, and no trace fix lies inside its geometry). It reports intersects_route false and covers the CTE between Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 and the SLE, a corridor this trip never enters. Under POL-RD-03 an advisory covering a corridor the optimal route never uses exonerates nothing, so the CTE point is discarded and the driver's case stands on the clean PIE advisory alone.

Nothing on this record engages the mandatory-escalation triggers in POL-RD-10: the trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) (100% coverage, maximum gap 0 s, steady 10 s sampling); no timestamps disagree or run backwards; the computed refund of $3.60 is far below the $150 ceiling; and no charge line is unmatched (ERP is zero throughout). The case is ripe for a monetary ruling and should not be held.
